title: Gold Rebounds 9% in August as Safe-Haven Appeal Returns After Iran War Selloff
excerpt: Bullion climbs back toward $4,400 per ounce as softer U.S. inflation, a weakening dollar, and signs of renewed central bank buying reverse months of war-driven losses.
body:
• Gold has rebounded 9% in August to around $4,400 per ounce, reclaiming ground lost during the sharp selloff triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran that began in late February.
  • A weaker dollar and softer inflation data have reduced Fed rate hike expectations, with markets now pricing just a 33% chance of a September increase, down from 55% a week ago.
  • Analysts see signs of central bank and institutional buying, with Chinese gold premiums and Asian trading hub demand pointing to renewed accumulation.
  • The 200-day moving average at $4,504 remains a key resistance level, and oil price volatility from the Iran conflict poses the main downside risk.

Gold is staging its strongest monthly rally since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began six months ago, climbing 9% in August to around $4,400 per ounce as easing inflation data and a weakening dollar draw institutional buyers back to the metal.

The rebound marks a turning point for bullion, which plunged from a record high of $5,595 per ounce in January to below $4,000 in June as the conflict drove up oil prices, fueled inflation fears, and prompted some central banks to sell gold reserves to support their domestic economies, according to Reuters.

The Handbrake Comes Off

"It feels as though the handbrake has finally been released from gold."

— Ross Norman, independent analyst

Gold has broken above two key technical resistance levels this month, crossing the 100-day moving average at $4,387 and sustaining gains above $4,400. On August 12, spot gold touched its highest level since June 5 at $4,406.64 per ounce.

The rally has been underpinned by a cascade of soft U.S. economic data. The economy unexpectedly lost jobs in July, consumer inflation eased to 3.4% from 3.5%, and the Producer Price Index came in flat against expectations for a 0.2% increase. Markets now price a 33% probability of a Fed rate hike in September, down from 55% a week earlier, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

"As we expect the Fed not to raise interest rates, gold price therefore still has further upside potential," Commerzbank said in a note.

Institutions Rebuild Positions

The speed and scale of gold's rebound suggest more than just retail interest. James Steel, chief precious metals analyst at HSBC, said the rally's strength implies that central banks or sovereign wealth funds may have been active buyers, though he cautioned this remained an inference rather than confirmed knowledge.

"It is really, I think, the rebuilding of positions that large institutions had before the conflict with Iran," Steel told Reuters.

Premiums in Asian trading hubs support that view. In China, the gold premium stood at $1.50 per ounce last week, pointing to renewed physical demand. Gold-backed ETFs added $7 billion to reach $582 billion in assets under management in the first half of August, according to the World Gold Council, though flows remain well below pre-war levels.

Oil Remains the Biggest Risk

The primary threat to gold's recovery is oil prices. Transit through the Strait of Hormuz has ground to a near-standstill after fresh attacks on shipping, and the United States has said it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely. Rising energy costs would reignite inflation fears and push the Fed toward tightening — a toxic combination for non-yielding bullion.

"If oil doesn't steal the show again, if the situation in the Middle East does not erupt and oil prices spike, then it looks as if the path of least resistance for gold is higher."

— James Steel, HSBC

Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange, echoed the concern. "If oil prices continue to rise, that's going to be a bearish element for the metals market because it would aid inflation and prompt central banks to raise interest rates," he said.

Meanwhile, gold discounts in India widened to more than two-month highs, reflecting elevated domestic prices that have dampened local demand.

What to Watch

The 200-day moving average, currently at $4,504, represents the next major hurdle for gold. Technical signals suggest the metal is approaching near-term overbought levels, which could cap gains in the short term.

Traders will parse the Fed's July meeting minutes on Wednesday for signals on the rate path. A continued decline in the dollar and stable oil prices would support the recovery, but any escalation in the Iran conflict — or data that revives rate-hike expectations — could quickly reverse the rebound.

Spot silver climbed 0.7% to $64.88 per ounce on Friday and was poised for a weekly gain, while platinum added 1.8% to $1,746.97.
